mcp_tools.name: list_vaults
mcp_tools.description: List the vaults on this Storm server, with their ids, names and note counts. Call this first — every other tool needs a vault id.

mcp_tools.name: get_vault
mcp_tools.description: Describe one vault: its note count, its folders, and the description its owner wrote for it.

mcp_tools.name: search
mcp_tools.description: Full-text search one vault, returning matching notes with a highlighted snippet from each. The fastest way to find a note.

mcp_tools.name: get_note
mcp_tools.description: Read one note in full: its markdown content and its metadata.

mcp_tools.name: get_related_notes
mcp_tools.description: Notes related to this one: those linking to it, and those sharing its tags. Every relation is exact and says why it is one — there is no semantic guessing here.

mcp_tools.name: list_tags
mcp_tools.description: Every tag in a vault with how many notes carry it.

mcp_tools.name: recent_notes
mcp_tools.description: Notes opened most recently, across every vault. Good for 'what was I working on'.

mcp_tools.name: get_note_history
mcp_tools.description: A note's revision history: version numbers, when each was written and by which device. Content is not included — fetch one with get_note_version.

mcp_tools.name: get_note_version
mcp_tools.description: The full text of one earlier revision of a note.

mcp_tools.name: session_context
mcp_tools.description: Read this agent session's launch context: the note it was started from (`context`) and its role note (`role`), each with vault and note ids, title, path, version and full markdown, or null when not set. A note deleted since is null and named in `missing`. Takes no arguments.

mcp_tools.name: list_scripts
mcp_tools.description: The kit vault's canonical scripts: names, sizes, modified times, Sorted. Optionally filter to one topic with prefix (e.g. 'psi-item-import/').

mcp_tools.name: get_script
mcp_tools.description: Fetch one canonical script from the kit vault by name (relative to its 'scripts/' root): its full text, size and vault-relative path.

mcp_tools.name: create_note
mcp_tools.description: Create a new note. Fails if the path is already taken. The note is stamped `source: ai` in its frontmatter so it is obvious later who wrote it.

mcp_tools.name: update_note
mcp_tools.description: Replace a note's content. Requires the base_version you read, so a note edited elsewhere is merged rather than overwritten. If the result says merged or conflict, the returned content is the server's — re-read before editing again.

mcp_tools.name: delete_note
mcp_tools.description: Delete a note. Storm has no trash: the file is removed from the vault immediately. Only the server's version history still holds the text.

mcp_tools.name: create_script
mcp_tools.description: Create a canonical script in the kit vault — the one place agents may store runnable code. name is relative to the vault's 'scripts/' root and must end in an allowed extension; content is the full text. Fails if the name is already taken; use update_script to change one. Scripts cannot be stored in any other vault.

mcp_tools.name: update_script
mcp_tools.description: Replace an existing script in the kit vault. name must end in an allowed extension; content is the full text. Fails if no such script exists — use create_script to add one.

storm_server.help:
Storm sync server

Usage: storm-server [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  serve            Run the sync server (what systemd starts)
  up               Install and start the server as a service. Linux: write the env file and enable the systemd unit (as root). macOS: install a LaunchAgent that runs as you, with the notes in ~/Storm (decision 84d; not root)
  down             Stop the service (and keep it from starting again)
  status           Show the service's state and a local health probe
  uninstall        macOS: stop the LaunchAgent and remove what `up` installed, keeping the notes. Linux: the package owns the install (`apt remove`)
  dry-run          Report what an import would change, then exit without writing
  passwd           Set the account's password — the recovery path when it is forgotten (A11). On a Storm not set up yet, this creates the account
  single-user      Choose which account a pre-v6 server keeps when it becomes single-user (decision 82). Only needed when it has no active owner to keep
  pair             Print a bootstrap pairing QR code for a fresh server (no account yet)
  has-account      Exit 0 if this Storm has its account, 1 if not (decision 84). For the installer, which waits on a first device's pairing
  host-enrollment  Mint a one-time Runtime Host enrollment string for a host on this machine, and print it for `storm-runtime enroll` to read (decision 84e). Run by whoever owns the state directory, like `passwd`. It is a secret, so it is printed only into a pipe, never to a terminal
  qr               Draw TEXT as a scannable QR block, for the installer's download and web links
  backup-db        Snapshot every vault index into DIR, then exit
  storage-root     Print the storage root this server uses, from its registry
  backup           Back up the vaults, the indexes and the account into `DEST/<YYYY-MM-DD>/`, check the snapshots open, and prune old ones: `deploy/storm-backup.sh` without bash, for Windows' nightly task (decision 99, W-S3)
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --log-file <FILE>  Append the log to this file instead of the terminal. Windows' windowless `storm-serverw` has no terminal (decision 99, W-S1)
  -h, --help             Print help
  -V, --version          Print version

commands.name: serve
commands.summary: Run the sync server (what systemd starts)
commands.help:
Run the sync server (what systemd starts)

Usage: storm-server serve [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --vault-root <VAULT_ROOT>
          Storage root — a directory holding one directory per vault
          
          [env: STORM_VAULT_ROOT=]

      --vault <VAULT>
          Deprecated: a single vault directory.
          
          Accepted for one release so an existing single-vault deployment starts without edits. The storage root becomes this directory's *parent* and this one directory is registered as a vault.

      --state <STATE>
          State directory for the registry and the per-vault SQLite indexes. Kept out of the vaults so they stay pure markdown
          
          [default: ./state]

      --host <HOST>
          [default: 127.0.0.1]

      --port <PORT>
          [default: 8484]

      --web <WEB>
          Directory holding the built Flutter web client, served at `/`

      --mcp
          Serve the Model Context Protocol endpoint at `/mcp`.
          
          Read-only tools over the same vaults and the same bearer token. Off by default: it is a new surface on the notes, and turning one on should be a decision rather than a side effect of upgrading.

      --no-discovery
          Do not advertise on the local network, and refuse pairing with the password, whatever the app's setting says (decision 118). Also `STORM_DISCOVERY=0`

      --log-file <FILE>
          Append the log to this file instead of the terminal. Windows' windowless `storm-serverw` has no terminal (decision 99, W-S1)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

storm_runtime.help:
Storm Runtime Host

Usage: storm-runtime <COMMAND>

Commands:
  enroll           Enroll this host with a Storm Server
  serve            Run the host: connect to the server and run the agents it asks for
  mcp-bridge       The agent's stdio MCP server for one gateway connection. Started by the agent CLI from the session's MCP config, never by hand: it reads its session handle and the daemon's socket from the environment, and holds no credential
  mcp-connect      An external MCP client's stdio server for a Storm Server's `/mcp` (Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop start it). Verifies the server's identity before sending anything
  harness-session  Tells the host which conversation the agent is on, so Storm can resume it. Run by the agent's own hook or plugin, never by hand; reads the id from stdin (a Claude Code hook's input) when none is given
  install          Install this host as a system service, as root. macOS: creates the `_stormruntime` account and `/Library/StormRuntime`, and loads the LaunchDaemon, which runs the host once it is enrolled. Windows (in an elevated shell): creates `C:\ProgramData\StormRuntime` and the `StormRuntime` service, which enrolling starts. Re-run it to upgrade. On Linux the package does this
  uninstall        Remove the system service `install` set up, as root (elevated on Windows). Workspaces are always kept
  check            Check this host's enrollment: verify the server, prove the key, and ask the server who it thinks this host is
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

commands.name: enroll
commands.summary: Enroll this host with a Storm Server
commands.help:
Enroll this host with a Storm Server.

Reads the enrollment string the app showed you from stdin, or prompts for it without echo. **Never pass it as an argument**: it carries a single-use secret, and arguments are visible to every user in `ps`.

Usage: storm-runtime enroll [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --state <STATE>
          [env: STORM_RUNTIME_STATE=]
          [default: /var/lib/storm-runtime]

      --name <NAME>
          How this host appears in the app. Defaults to the hostname

      --force
          Replace an existing enrollment

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

commands.name: serve
commands.summary: Run the host: connect to the server and run the agents it asks for
commands.help:
Run the host: connect to the server and run the agents it asks for

Usage: storm-runtime serve [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --state <STATE>      [env: STORM_RUNTIME_STATE=] [default: /var/lib/storm-runtime]
      --config <CONFIG>    [env: STORM_RUNTIME_CONFIG=] [default: /etc/storm-runtime/runtime.toml]
      --exclusive-account  Declare that this account runs nothing but this host (AM37): at startup and after shutdown, end every other process of it. Passed by the packaged service definitions; refused unless running as the service account, and never as root
  -h, --help               Print help

commands.name: mcp-connect
commands.summary: An external MCP client's stdio server for a Storm Server's `/mcp` (Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop start it). Verifies the server's identity before sending anything
commands.help:
An external MCP client's stdio server for a Storm Server's `/mcp` (Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop start it). Verifies the server's identity before sending anything.

The key is read from STORM_MCP_KEY or --key-file, **never an argument**: arguments are visible to every user in `ps`.

Usage: storm-runtime mcp-connect [OPTIONS] --server <SERVER> --pk <PK>

Options:
      --server <SERVER>
          The server's id (`srv_…`), as the app shows it

      --pk <PK>
          The server's public key, unpadded base64url, as the app shows it

      --addr <ADDR>
          The server's own address, e.g. `http://192.168.1.10:8484`. Optional when a --relay is given

      --relay <RELAYS>
          A relay that reaches the server (`wss://…`). Repeatable. Only a seed: the server's current relays are learned on each connect and cached

      --key-file <KEY_FILE>
          A file holding the `stk_` key, instead of STORM_MCP_KEY

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
